label: Early result
confidence_note: Traffic is fitted to measured car counts at the surrounding junctions, but no counter measures the closed lane itself, routes are inferred, and signal timings are guessed.

cars.summary: About 755 to 871 drivers over the works period (7am to 10pm) use the block as a shortcut from La Trobe St to A'Beckett St and must go another way. If cars can't turn right from La Trobe St into Swanston St, it is about 77. Most drive no further, some up to about 320 m. The change in total travel time is too small to separate from run-to-run variation.

public_transport.summary: Trams are in the street network but no tram services were simulated.

pedestrians.summary: SUMO can model pedestrians, but this run covers cars only.

trucks.summary: All vehicles are simulated as cars. Trucks are not modelled on their own.

assumptions: Every hour of the works, 7am to 10pm on a weekday, simulated separately after a 30 minute warm-up, and added up. The busiest hour for diversions is 5pm to 6pm.
Street network from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors), built with SUMO netconvert. Signal timings are guessed, not the real SCATS plans.

Traffic fitted to car counts per approach from SCATS stop-line detectors at the 9 junctions around the closure (August 2026 weekdays, detector roles from DTP signal sheets), and to 43 other CBD signal sites, using SUMO routeSampler. Whole-site SCATS totals also count bikes, trams and queue loops, so the other sites' totals were cut to 57%, the car share found at the measured junctions.
All of the counted traffic was inserted. The fitted traffic matches 99% of counted streets within the usual tolerance (GEH under 5) in every hour.
Closure: the only car lane on Swanston St between La Trobe St and Little La Trobe St (208489241, northbound) is closed. The rest of the block is tram only in OpenStreetMap, as on the street.

That lane is the only car entry to Little La Trobe St and the east end of A'Beckett St, so the closure cuts car access to them. Trips ending there are removed from both runs rather than counted (0 in this demand).

Diversions: no counter measures the closed lane. Routes fitted to the counts plan 67 trips through it over the works period (7am to 10pm), but in normal runs 755 to 871 drivers use it as a shortcut around queues. The range is those drivers. Measured counts cap it: every car entering the block comes from La Trobe St, which carries 11,686 cars over the works period (7am to 10pm), both directions together (SCATS detectors at site 2921).

The shortcut needs a right turn from westbound La Trobe St into Swanston St. The signal plan for site 2921 shows no car right-turn signal there, only a bike hook turn. The same runs with that turn banned give 71 to 92 drivers (median 77), which is the low end of the range.
Detour: the low value is the shortest way round for these drivers. Typical and high are the extra distance they actually drove with the block closed (median and upper quartile), with live rerouting.
Up to 16% of cars could not enter the network within 5 minutes and were dropped. Delay is likely understated.

Delay is the extra travel time of the same trips with and without the closure, for all trips over the works period (7am to 10pm), across 5 random seeds. Two normal runs differ by up to 318 vehicle-hours on their own, and the closure runs differ from normal by -521 to 284, so no delay is reported (like queue, it would be rated on noise).
Queue growth could not be separated from run-to-run variation. Normal runs differ from each other by up to 205 m on their worst lane, so no queue is reported.
Cars stuck for 5 minutes are moved on by SUMO (teleported). Up to 167 teleports in a closure run.
Trams keep running in reality, but no tram services were simulated, so tram delays are not included.
